request_state.conjecture: Beal: A^x + B^y = C^z with x,y,z >= 3 and gcd(gcd(A,B),C) = 1 has no solutions. Audit has shown three recurring failure modes in this project: conflating a residual mod-p congruence with an isogeny or l-adic statement; using a Chabauty rank bound over a base field to conclude about points of higher degree; and relabelling a GRH-conditional or heuristic result as unconditional.

obligations: U110 p=17 analysis assumes FINITENESS OF SHA for its Cassels-Tate parity step, then reports rank J_{17,1}(K) = 2 exactly; Sha finiteness is open
U110 concedes rank 2 defeats standard one-generator Chabauty-Coleman, so p=17 is NOT closed

U102 claim that x^5+y^5=z^11 and z^13 are unconditionally resolved is INVALID (U113 Part IV): it removes GRH using Cohen-Martinet heuristics and GRH-conditional Bach bounds. Those cases remain GRH-conditional as Dahmen-Siksek left them
Dahmen-Siksek (Acta Arith. 164:65-100, 2014) cited repeatedly across the project and NEVER checked against the primary source
trivial solution persistence for p in {17,19,23} analysed but not eliminated

evaluations.citation_audit_PRIMARY_SOURCE: CONFIRMED 2026-09-17: Dahmen-Siksek, Acta Arith. 164 (2014) 65-100 (arXiv:1309.4030) prove (5,5,7), (5,5,19), (7,7,5) UNCONDITIONALLY and (5,5,11), (5,5,13), (7,7,11) ASSUMING GRH. This confirms U113 Part IV: U102 claim to have removed GRH for p=11,13 is the sole step between conditional and unconditional, and that removal is circular. Checked against abstract and bibliographic record, NOT full text.

candidate_A.novelty_note: Distinct base field and Frey family from the (3,3,p) route; failure mode would be newform persistence rather than sieve exhaustion.
candidate_A.claim: A^5 + B^5 = C^p has no primitive nontrivial solutions for primes p >= 5, via Hilbert modular forms over Q(sqrt 5).
candidate_A.method: BCDF Frey elliptic curve families E_{a,b}, F_{a,b} over F = Q(sqrt 5) (h_F = h_F^+ = 1), level lowering to Hilbert newforms at levels dividing 40, 64, 80 and p_2^6, with an a_3-dichotomy.

obligations: [L:Q] = 20 so the descent field over L has degree 340 over Q; U99 degree-34 case ALREADY cannot be certified unconditionally (Minkowski bound 5.67e19, bnfcertify fails), so degree 340 is hopeless by this route
rank can only grow in extensions, so rank_Z J^-(L) >= rank_Z J^-(k)
naive symmetric-power Chabauty needs rank < g - d + 1 = 8 - 10 + 1 < 0 for d=10: IMPOSSIBLE, ruled out immediately
U99 rank bound over k is itself conditional on GRH + Cohen-Martinet (U113 Part IV), so even the base case is not unconditional
candidate_B.novelty_note: First candidate to target the correct field. Its most likely failure is computational infeasibility at degree 340, which would itself be an informative obstruction and would push the weighted route back to the modular method.
candidate_B.claim: rank_Z J^-(L) < 8 where L is the degree-10 extension of k = Q(sqrt5) generated by a root of x^10 + 256, so that Chabauty-Coleman applies to C^-(L) - the field that actually contains the points coming from solutions of X^10 + 256 Y^10 = Z^17.
candidate_B.method: Redo the U99 2-descent and Selmer rank bound over L instead of over k, or replace it with symmetric-power Chabauty / a covering collection over k of the degree-10 points.

compatible.instructions: Are these two research candidates mathematically COMPATIBLE, in the sense that the objects, fields, exponents and equations they concern are the same or are related by a reduction that the project has already proved?

criteria.true: they concern the same equation, signature, curve or field, or one supplies an input the other consumes
criteria.false: they concern unrelated equations, signatures or methods, so no joint statement could be formed without inventing a new reduction

combination_value.instructions: If these two candidates were combined into a single line of attack, how much would the combination accomplish beyond what the better of the two accomplishes alone?
criteria: level 0: nothing; the combination is just the stronger candidate restated, or they are incompatible
level 1: the combination tidies bookkeeping but resolves no obligation that either one leaves open
level 2: one candidate discharges a specific open obligation recorded in the other
level 3: the combination closes a case or an infinite family that neither one closes alone

shared_failure.instructions: Would these two candidates FAIL FOR THE SAME REASON, so that combining them adds no diversity of failure mechanism and a single obstruction would defeat both?

criteria.true: both depend on the same blocked step, the same unverified citation, or the same one of the three recorded failure modes
criteria.false: they would fail for different reasons, so each provides genuine independent information
